order: Apply the round-3 findings from the owner-requested holistic review of WO-11. First, strike the 7d maxStaleMs ruled in round 1 and replace it with a 48h ceiling — a weekly allowance moves too fast for a week-old reading to count as evidence — while the 24h maxFreshMs window stands as ruled. Second, carry the staleness disclosure onto the published bucket-state object (stale, ageMs), not only the human report, so a snapshot consumer or the dispatcher sees it too. Third, ledger the outstanding exercise debt and commit the round-3 verdicts and band records. Make the disclosure purely additive. Staleness is disclosed, not discounted — publish the recorded fraction exactly as read, leave reserveBreached, throttleObserved and exhausted computed the way they are today, and let no bucket's routed pool state change merely because its reading is stale. Do not modify router/router.js; the router keeps ownership of the ladder and the reserve formula.
claims: The window moves to 48h, the 24h fresh band is untouched, and the disclosure keys were added on top of the published state object rather than in place of anything. The routing-relevant fields there are computed exactly as before, so no bucket's routed pool state moves because a reading is stale, and router/router.js was not opened. Round-3 verdicts, band records and the outstanding exercise debt are all committed. Verified with node tests/quartermaster.test.js, 191 passed, and node tests/router.test.js, 135 passed.
